In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of miRs in human cancer.
the identification of miRs involved in breast cancer progression and metastasis.
understanding the role of miR‐148 and its target genes in breast cancer and the mechanisms by which miR‐148 controls the expression of these target genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

miR148b plays a key role in the regulation of the metastatic process of breast cancer, by targeting a set of genes involved in the control of cell adhesion, survival, and migration, and by regulating the expression of a number of other miRs.

miR‐148a/b are involved in breast cancer development, and in particular in its metastatic dissemination, by coordinating the activity of several genes, including ITGA5, PIK3, ROCK1, NRAS, CSF1, and others, which are involved in cell migration, survival, invasion, angiogenesis, and immune response.
the miR‐148‐3p/‐5p signature is a prognostic biomarker for breast cancer patients, and miR‐148a/‐148b/‐152 cluster is a major coordinator in the control of tumor progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel microRNA, miR‐149, that is down‐regulated in a large fraction of primary breast tumors.

miR148b, which is down‐regulated in primary tumors, has a major role in controlling breast cancer progression by targeting several genes involved in the regulation of cell adhesion, migration, survival, and invasion.
the miR‐148a‐148b cluster is involved in breast cancer progression and metastasis by coordinating a novel signaling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the miR‐148 family, in particular miR‐148a and miR‐148, are major coordinators of breast cancer malignancy and progression and that they can be used as a prognostic tool for breast cancer patients.
miR148b, a microRNA (miR) that we found down-regulated in aggressive breast cancers, has a major role in the control of malignancy.
a relapse‐specific signature of 16 miRs can be used to predict the clinical outcome of breast cancer patients.
